set.title: ESAT Mathematics 1 — First 10
set.authorship: Original questions. Informed by the official ESAT Mathematics 1 specification and the style of historic NSAA/ENGAA papers; no question has been copied.
designIntent: A strong first-use set: accessible opening, rising challenge, no throwaway questions.
Each question is intended to turn on one clear idea and remain workable under admissions-test time pressure.
Distractors correspond to identifiable mistakes and can be used for targeted feedback.

questions.stemMarkdown:
A rectangular tank measures \(0.8	ext{ m}\) by \(0.5	ext{ m}\) by \(0.45	ext{ m}\). It is \(80\%\) full of water.

Water is removed at a constant rate of \(12\) litres per minute.

How long does it take to empty the tank?

solution.title: Use the amount of water actually in the tank.

distractorMap.reason: Uses the empty 20% of the tank instead of the water present.
Finds 12 minutes, then labels it as seconds.
Applies the 80% factor twice.
Calculates the time for a completely full tank.
Correct.
Treats the 144 litres as a time in seconds.

questions.stemMarkdown: Which of the following is equal to\n\n\[\frac{3+\sqrt5}{\sqrt5-1}\,?\]

distractorMap.reason: A familiar surd value, but it does not come from this fraction.
Uses the wrong sign after multiplying by the conjugate.
Stops before dividing the numerator by 4.
Correct.
Divides the constant term incorrectly.
Changes the denominator but leaves the numerator untouched.

questions.stemMarkdown: A shop increases a price by \(25\%\). It then discounts the increased price so that the final price is \(10\%\) below the original price.\n\nWhat is the discount?

solution.title: Compare both prices with the same original price.
stepsMarkdown: Let the original price be \(P\). The increased price is \(1.25P\).

distractorMap.reason: Uses the final 10% reduction from the original price as the shop's discount.
Subtracts the two percentage changes: \(25-10\).
Correct.
Uses the 35 percentage-point gap between 125% and 90%, but divides by the wrong base.
This is the percentage of the increased price that remains, not the discount.
This is the final price as a percentage of the original price.

questions.stemMarkdown: For values of \(x\) for which the expression is defined, simplify\n\n\[\frac{2x^2-5x-3}{4x^2-9}\div\frac{x-3}{2x+3}.\]

solution.title: Factor first, then turn the division into multiplication.
stepsMarkdown: Cancel the common factors to get \(\dfrac{2x+1}{2x-3}\).

distractorMap.reason: Does not fully invert the second fraction before multiplying.
Cancels the wrong factor from the first numerator.
Takes the reciprocal of the final answer.
Cancels \(x-3\) but does not use the reciprocal correctly.
Cancels factors across the division sign before rewriting it as multiplication.
Correct.

questions.stemMarkdown:
The first five terms of a sequence are

\[3,\ 8,\ 17,\ 30,\ 47.\]

Which expression gives the \(n\)th term?

solution.title: The constant second difference fixes the quadratic term.
stepsMarkdown: Second differences: \(4,4,4\), so the leading term is \(2n^2\).
Subtracting \(2n^2\) from the sequence leaves \(1,0,-1,-2,-3\), which is \(2-n\).

distractorMap.reason: Uses a leading coefficient of 1, which would give second differences of 2.
Correct.
Gets the quadratic coefficient right but misses the required correction.
Has the right quadratic coefficient but already gives 5 when \(n=1\).
Matches the first two terms only; the later terms drift away.
Treats the sequence as linear even though the first differences change.

solution.title: Use the two smaller similar triangles.

Copies the shorter hypotenuse segment.

This is the other leg of the 9–12–15 triangle, not the altitude.
Adds the two parts of the hypotenuse.

solution.title: Split the bottom side into three horizontal pieces.
stepsMarkdown: Add both runs and the top side: \(AD=6\sqrt3+4+6\).

distractorMap.reason: Correct.
Omits the 6 cm horizontal run on the right.
Halves the left-hand horizontal run.
Adds the perpendicular height as an extra horizontal length.
Uses \(6\tan30^\circ\) instead of \(6\div\tan30^\circ\).
Uses the 45° triangle's hypotenuse instead of its horizontal side.

questions.stemMarkdown: A bag contains 3 red counters, 2 blue counters and 1 green counter. Two counters are chosen at random without replacement.\n\nWhat is the probability that **exactly one counter is red, or the two counters are the same colour**?

solution.title: Count unordered pairs.
stepsMarkdown: Exactly one red: choose 1 of 3 red and 1 of 3 non-red counters, giving \(3\times3=9\) pairs.
The two cases do not overlap, so the probability is \(\dfrac{9+4}{15}=\dfrac{13}{15}\).

distractorMap.reason: Counts only the same-colour pairs.
Counts only pairs containing exactly one red counter.
Counts the two possible same-colour labels rather than the four actual pairs.
Includes red-red but misses the blue-blue pair.
Correct.
Assumes the two stated cases cover every possible pair; red-blue and red-green do, but blue-green does not.

questions.stemMarkdown:
The table describes a histogram of the times, \(t\) minutes, taken by 50 students to finish a task.

| Time \(t\) (minutes) | Frequency density |
|---|---:|
| \(0<t\le10\) | \(1.2\) |
| \(10<t\le20\) | \(2.0\) |
| \(20<t\le40\) | \(0.9\) |

What is the estimated median time?

solution.title: Turn density into frequency before locating the median.
stepsMarkdown: The median is the 25th value, so it lies in \(10<t\le20\).
It is the \(25-12=13\)th of the 20 values in that class.

distractorMap.reason: Uses half the median position as though it were a time.
Takes the midpoint of the median class without using the frequencies.
Correct.
Places 15 rather than 13 of the class's 20 values below the median.
Uses the upper boundary of the median class.
Confuses the median's position in the ordered list with its time value.

questions.stemMarkdown: A rectangle has perimeter \(34\text{ cm}\) and diagonal length \(13\text{ cm}\).\n\nWhat is its area?

solution.title: Use the sum of the side lengths and the diagonal together.
stepsMarkdown: Let the side lengths be \(a\) and \(b\). From the perimeter, \(a+b=17\).

distractorMap.reason: Finds \(2ab=120\), then divides by 4 rather than 2.
Correct.
Takes half of the diagonal squared.
Finds \(2ab\) but forgets the final division by 2.
Uses the diagonal squared as the rectangle's area.
Uses \((a+b)^2\) as the area.
